title: Iceberg reads binary equality deletes and snapshots a nested byte slice
summary: A real Parquet equality delete left IDs 200 and 201 alongside 203 on the parent. The merged table scan returned only 203. A copied nested binary slice also retained AB after a source mutation and preserved the source position.

change.description: The generic reader can reuse storage while reading successive delete keys.

notes: The table format is v2, the physical data and delete files are Parquet, and the scan projects only the integer ID.
Each deployment checks the JDK fingerprint, ordered artifact digests, caller classes and original class providers. The same compiled caller runs both sides in fresh JVMs.
